entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God who planted the garden.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and designates the same God.
בְּעֵדֶן identifies Eden as the place where Yahweh God planted the garden for the man he had formed.

review.translation: [Now|0] [Yahweh|1] [God|2] [had planted|0] [a garden|3] [in Eden|4], [in the east|5], [and|6] [there|7] [he put|6] [the man|9,8] [whom|10] [he had formed|11].

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּטַּע, גַּן is its direct object, and בְּעֵדֶן identifies where he planted the garden.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־. The initial נ of the root assimilates to ט, marked by the dagesh in טּ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּטַּע יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים גַּן, יַהְוֶה names the one who planted the garden. אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to the name.
analysis.morphology: Singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they form the subject of the singular verb וַיִּטַּע, identifying Yahweh God as the one who planted the garden.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: גַּן is the direct object of וַיִּטַּע ‘he planted’. The phrase בְּעֵדֶן ‘in Eden’ locates the garden, and שָׁם ‘there’ refers back to the place where God put the man.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In גַּן בְּעֵדֶן, גַּן names what Yahweh God planted, and בְּעֵדֶן says where he planted it. The following שָׁם, “there,” refers back to that location.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ, “in,” is prefixed to the singular proper noun עֵדֶן.
analysis.sense: Eden, the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.

analysis.evidence: מִקֶּדֶם follows גַּן בְּעֵדֶן, “a garden in Eden,” and further locates the garden. The next clause says God placed the man שָׁם, “there,” reinforcing the spatial reading.
analysis.morphology: Preposition מִן prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun. The נ assimilates to the following ק, marked by dagesh.

analysis.evidence: YHWH God continues as the subject. אֶת־הָאָדָם marks the man as the direct object, and שָׁם (“there”) refers to the garden God had just planted.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם, “he placed the man there,” שָׁם identifies where God placed the man. It refers back to גַּן בְּעֵדֶן, “a garden in Eden.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם, “he placed the man there,” אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the definite direct object of וַיָּשֶׂם.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the direct object of וַיָּשֶׂם ‘he placed’. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר יָצָר ‘whom he had formed’ identifies him as the particular man God had formed.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָצָר, “the man whom he formed,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause in which הָאָדָם is the understood object of יָצָר.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָצָר, “the man whom he had formed,” the man is the object of יָצָר and יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is its subject. The relative clause recalls the shaping of the man from dust in Genesis 2:7.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, in pausal form
